3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("psych", "effectsize", "ggplot2"))
library(psych)
library(effectsize)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# === 01 · Paired t-test ===
print(psych::describe(data.frame(a = d[["sleep_baseline"]], b = d[["sleep_high"]])))
res <- t.test(d[["sleep_baseline"]], d[["sleep_high"]], paired = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided")
print(res)
effectsize::cohens_d(d[["sleep_baseline"]], d[["sleep_high"]], paired = TRUE)
pl <- data.frame(case = rep(seq_along(d[["sleep_baseline"]]), 2),
  cond = factor(rep(c("sleep_baseline", "sleep_high"), each = length(d[["sleep_baseline"]])), levels = c("sleep_baseline", "sleep_high")),
  value = c(d[["sleep_baseline"]], d[["sleep_high"]]))
print(ggplot(pl, aes(cond, value, group = case)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#9cc2ec") + geom_point(colour = "#0c447c") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL))

LaTeX source (report.tex)
\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}

\usepackage{booktabs,graphicx,siunitx}

\begin{document}

\section{Paired t-test}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
Condition & N & M & SD \\
\midrule
sleep\_baseline & 40 & 7.40 & 0.45 \\
sleep\_high & 40 & 6.20 & 0.72 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{llllllll}
\toprule
Pair & t & df & p & Mdiff & 95\% CI & d [95\% CI]z & r (paired) \\
\midrule
sleep\_baseline $-$ sleep\_high & 14.14 & 39 & $<$.001 & 1.20 & [1.03, 1.38] & 2.24 [1.65, 2.81] & 0.66 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\includegraphics{figures/01_paired-t-test/figure_difference.png}

Tests whether the average change between two related measurements (e.g. before vs. after) differs from zero. A p below alpha means a significant change; the mean difference, CI and dz describe its size (their sign depends on the subtraction order, A$-$B). A p at or above alpha does not prove there was no change --- only that none was detected. Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05.

A paired-samples t-test gave M=1.2, t(39)=14.14, p $<$ .001, dz=2.24 [1.65, 2.81].

Statistical basis: Paired-samples t-test (Student (1908). "The probable error of a mean." Biometrika, 6(1), 1-25.); Cohen's dz effect size (Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Routledge.); Paired correlation (Pearson r) between the two conditions (Pearson, K. (1895). "Note on regression and inheritance in the case of two parents." Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, 58, 240-242.).

\end{document}

Harness README
# 06 · Paired t-test

**Question:** do two related measurements differ?

**Scenario:** Sleep & caffeine: does a high dose reduce sleep quality versus baseline?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `sleep-caffeine.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** two-tailed; α 0.05; 95% CI

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `sleep_baseline` | condition A |
| `sleep_high` | condition B |
